title: Timing canaries around FI-critical blocks (software Instruction Timer) and write→jitter→readback of the clock tree and TZ configuration
threat: CfiCounter catches skipped steps but not clock-glitch or stuck-at faults that leave the counter intact; the RCC/PLL setup is itself a fault target (μ-Glitch had to glitch the L5 PLL config to get under the BoD), and while sau.rs has a post-write readback the RCC path has none and neither inserts a random delay before the readback.
proposal: (1) `fi::TimedWindow`: snapshot a secure-only TIM (or DWT CYCCNT with LAR unlocked, secured) at block entry, compute the expected cycle envelope at build time per block (min/max with RDI jitter budget), and on exit require entry+min ≤ now ≤ entry+max through check_true_into_sentinel; apply to ct_eq of the two 4008-B sigs, verify-before-release, gated_unlock pre-commit → SE verdict, SCP03/CCM unwrap, SAU/GTZC/AIRCR setup and the first-boot RDP authorisation. Over/under-run ⇒ handle_fault (FI-05). (2) rcc.rs: after PLL/SWS switch, wait_random then re-read CFGR1/PLL1CFGR/PLL1DIVR and compare to the constants under a sentinel; mirror in the FSBL once it has a TRNG. (3) sau.rs: insert wait_random before each readback pass and add a second voted pass (read_volatile_voted) of SAU_RBAR/RLAR, GTZC SECCFGR and AIRCR, since the existing F6 verifier is a single pass.
rationale: NXP's LPC55 Code Watchdog pairs a secure counter with an instruction timer precisely because counters alone miss timing faults; RP2350's digital glitch detectors are the hardware form of the same idea. A software window on a secure timer is the closest U585 equivalent and is cheap. Readback after jitter is the standard answer to the μ-Glitch SAU/PLL targets.
repo_evidence: grep CYCCNT|DWT|timing canary secure/src → only test-key-speed register strings in main_sau_pure_tests.rs:1073-1099; no runtime canary
secure/src/sau.rs:401-409 (single-pass post-write readback verifier F6; no wait_random before it)
secure/src/fi.rs:199-252 (CfiCounter: control-flow only; doc admits 2-fault stack-write bypass)
vendor_precedent: NXP AN12912 Code Watchdog (Secure Counter + Instruction Timer); RP2350 datasheet §10.9 glitch detectors; μ-Glitch countermeasure (random 0–9 cycle pre-delay per fault target).
risks: Envelopes must absorb legitimate variance (C10 target-sum grinding spreads sign time by ±1 s, HASH DMA stalls, RDI jitter) — set them on measured distributions, not estimates, or they become a reliability bug; DWT is a debug resource and must be locked/secured so NS cannot reset CYCCNT. Adds flash to the already-over-budget ui-px image.
